Content: … Osei Kwadwo clearly believed that Asante [Ashanti] could not maintain its position solely by force of arms. During his `text(13-year)` reign (`1764–77`), he shifted authority in many areas from military leaders to civilian officials. The Asante devoted great care to the training of these administrators. Many officials entered government departments as children and spent `text(years)` performing menial [low-level] jobs as they absorbed the routines and attitudes of public service. Though most of these youths were the sons of officials, Osei Kwadwo saw to it that opportunities were created for talented outsiders. Trainees who showed ability were promoted, and the most capable eventually attained important posts. Under the guidance of these individuals, Asante entered the `19^text(th)` `text(century)` as the most sophisticated society in all of Africa. …
